subject: Procurement roadmap & compliance gating for CoreThera integration
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — Redwood <> CoreThera demo

Hi Liam —

Great to meet earlier (and thanks for the walkthrough of CoreThera's ML inference workload). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on procurement/compliance path: 

- Procurement route: you mentioned internal preference for a PO, and interest in marketplace for faster procurement if legal allows. Please confirm which path procurement would prefer as primary.
- Compliance gating: you flagged SOC 2 attestation and a DPA as must-haves. We can provide our SOC 2 Type II report and our standard DPA (we typically sign customer DPAs or addenda).
- Commercials: I attached a rate card snapshot; we have options for card payment for initial POC credits vs monthly PO for committed Dedicated capacity.
- Next meeting: propose a short call with your procurement + IT security to clarify timing and specific questionnaire items. Can you do Thu 5/13 10:00am PT?

Attachments: commercial_rate_card_Q2_2027.xlsx (rate card snapshot)

Action items for us: Marissa, can you prepare a one-page summary of payment/commitment options we can send to procurement? Ben, please flag any customer success onboarding notes relevant to PO timelines.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@corethera.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — Redwood <> CoreThera demo

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the summary and for the demo — team was impressed with the latency and rollout options. Quick answers: 

- Procurement: CoreThera's procurement team prefers PO for any committed spend. For an initial POC we could pay by card if the process is quicker, but any production work will need a standard PO/contract.
- Marketplace: we're open to marketplace if it shortens legal review, but procurement needs to confirm whether our finance systems will accept marketplace invoicing (we suspect it'll complicate VAT/accounting).
- Security: We require SOC 2 Type II and a signed DPA. We also maintain an RFP-style security questionnaire (attached to the procurement thread) — we can share the form ahead of the call.

Thu 5/13 10:00am PT works for procurement + IT security — I'll invite them.

I'll forward the questionnaire to you now.

Cheers,
Liam
Director of IT & Procurement | CoreThera
liam.oconnor@corethera.ai

Subject: Fwd: CoreThera questionnaire + asks (procurement playbook, SOC2/DPA)

Team — forwarding CoreThera's security questionnaire and procurement note. Highlights from the call: PO preferred for production; POC could be card; marketplace acceptable if procurement signs off. They need SOC 2 Type II and a signed DPA before procurement will issue a PO.

Rishi — can you confirm which version of our SOC 2 we can share publicly and whether any redaction is required? Also, can you draft suggested answers to the questionnaire sections on data residency, encryption, and incident response?

Marissa — please put together two short commercial options: (A) POC on card (month 1) then PO for month 2+; (B) 12-month committed Dedicated pricing with quarterly invoicing via PO. Include lead time for provisioning Dedicated capacity.

Ben — note for onboarding: typical PO-to-live timeline is 3–4 weeks once legal/DPA counters are agreed; include any quick wins to accelerate the POC.

I'll plan the Thu 10am PT call once Liam sends the invite.

Thanks,
Steph

Steph / team —

Quick status and deliverables I can own for the Thu call: 

1) SOC 2: We can share the full SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA or via a secure link. Attached is the redacted SOC2_Type2_2024.pdf that covers control objectives they asked about. If they need the full report we'll request a signed NDA and provide the original.

2) DPA: Attached is Redwood_DPA_v3.1.pdf — it's our standard customer DPA. Legal can accept a reasonable number of redlines; for procurement speed suggest we offer the standard DPA with a 30-day turnaround on requested changes.

3) Questionnaire: I'll draft suggested answers for the sections marked mandatory (data classification, encryption at rest/in transit, key management, logging/audit, incident response) and share as a separate doc by EOD.

4) Marketplace vs PO: from a security/compliance standpoint there's no difference; the gating items are the same — SOC 2 + DPA + answers to questionnaire. Accounting will handle whether marketplace invoicing is acceptable.

Attachments: SOC2_Type2_2024.pdf, Redwood_DPA_v3.1.pdf

Subject: Commercial options + next steps before procurement call

Hi Liam / Steph —

Per Steph's ask, attaching two quick commercial paths for CoreThera: 

Option A — POC-first (fast):
- Card payment for up to $10k usage in month 1
- No long-term commitment
- If moving to production: standard PO with monthly invoicing; provisioning time ~2 weeks from PO acceptance

Option B — Commitment (preferred for predictable cost):
- 12-month committed Dedicated pool, invoiced quarterly via PO
- Discounted unit rates per token/hour; onboarding provisioning ~3–4 weeks after PO/contract execution

We'll also bring a short statement of work template to the procurement call to accelerate approval.

Next steps: 1) Confirm if procurement will accept marketplace invoicing (Liam to confirm). 2) Rishi to share the questionnaire answers by EOD. 3) Steph to schedule Thu 10am PT call (Liam already confirmed).

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
